facts.statement: The researchers used a combination of genetic tools and behavioral tests on mice that drank alcohol for four weeks.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The study measured how much alcohol the mice drank and how anxious or depressed they appeared.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Turning on specific brain connections from the prelimbic cortex to the nucleus accumbens core lowered alcohol drinking and reduced signs of anxiety and depression.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Turning on connections from the infralimbic cortex to the amygdala lowered alcohol drinking and anxiety but did not affect depression-like behaviors.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: A protein analysis identified a specific molecule called PPP1R1B as important in the brain cells connecting the prelimbic cortex to the nucleus accumbens core.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: Changing the amount of PPP1R1B in the other set of brain cells affected alcohol use and anxiety but had no effect on depression.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The results show that different parts of the prefrontal cortex control alcohol use and emotional issues through separate pathways.
facts.subject: animals
